paras.text: The kamikaze hit on USS Haynsworth, on picket station 12 miles from Task Group 58.3's carriers off Okinawa, on the first day of Japan's mass kamikaze offensive. Her own reports beside the other ships of the group and the Japanese records of the planes sent against them. Hand-edited; every entry cites its page in `ref`.

- `events.yml`: every timed entry, US and Japanese, in Item time. - `positions.csv`: fixes, and positions given as bearing and distance from another (`from`, `brg`, `nm`). `hand-placed` rows are reference points placed on a modern map. - `claims.yml`: the evidence board. Each disputed question (when was she hit, what hit her, who flew it), each answer, and what kind of evidence it is.

The ship's track for April 1945 is in [`ships/dd-700-haynsworth/`](../../ships/dd-700-haynsworth/README.md). The crew lists stay out of these records (see the kit's rules on people); the casualty count and the Report of Casualties page are cited instead.

events.words: "At 1700 we took picket station #1, 12 miles bearing 060°T from our group."
Walker, Weeks and Haynsworth assigned picket stations; "enemy plans to attack in force tomorrow" (as quoted by Irons; not yet checked on the scan).
events.source: Irons, Phalanx, quoting Waldron's war diary

events.words: Task Force point option 26-50N 129-10E. Pickets for the day: Haynsworth #1 (060°); Weeks #2X (000°); Walker #12 (300°).
Two Saiun and an Army Type 100 scout leave to find the carriers. They report two groups (six carriers) south of Amami-Ōshima.
events.source: Fifth Air Fleet operations record, pp. 11-13

events.words: A Saiun reports 4 carriers at 「メツ三ス」, the 20-minute square 27-00N to 27-20N, 129-40E to 130-00E. Haynsworth's 0800 fix is 10-20 nm west of it.
events.source: Recon 11 message log and results table, pp. 23-29, 37-38

events.words: Eleven of the wounded are transferred to South Dakota on 6 April, three more on the 7th. By 9 April "five additional deaths" aboard her bring "the total to twelve (12)".

"Scattered to broken low type clouds. Scattered altocumulus. Ceiling generally unlimited. Visibility unrestricted. Surface winds northerly 8 to 16 knots. Flying conditions good. Moderate sea. No swell." Task Group 58.1 was a few miles east of 58.3.

events.original: 爆戦三〇機 彗星二三機 一〇一五—一三一〇間逐次発進
events.translation: 30 bomb-carrying Zeros and 23 Suisei take off one after another between 1015 and 1310.
events.note: Against the carrier force southeast of Amami-Ōshima.
events.source: Fifth Air Fleet operations record, pp. 11-13

events.words: Suisei unit, first attack: 11 Suisei from First Kokubu to search for and attack the carrier force (including 4 carriers) southeast of Amami-Ōshima, at 「メツミス」. Led by Lt. 野村浩三.
events.source: 210th Air Group action report, narrative, form p. 9

events.words: Dinah splashed by the task group's CAP at 330°-29 mi.
Four Suisei turn back (野村/矢島; 宮尾/佐守; 鈴木/新谷; 新屋/長嶺). The time reads 1015 or 1115.
events.source: 210th Air Group action report, form p. 9; crew list form p. 23

events.words: A second-stage search plane reports an enemy force including carriers at 「サキ四セ」, the 20-minute square 27-20N to 27-40N, 130-00E to 130-20E, about 40 nm north-east of Haynsworth's noon fix.
"Two JUDYs shot down by ESSEX CAP at 035-35": on Haynsworth's side of the group, 70 minutes before she was hit.
Zeke splashed at 350-16.
The 210th's fighter escort, over Amami at 1140, fights Hellcats about 80 nm south of Tokunoshima.
"One JUDY shot down by ESSEX CAP at 000-20".
Fix 26-55N 129-31E. South Dakota at 26-41-45N 129-25-30E.
events.source: Haynsworth war diary, p. 3; South Dakota war diary

events.words: Seven Zekes intercepted at 000-15; one to five splashed. Cabot: a large group intercepted 40 mi north, "CAP broke up the raid".
events.source: Essex chronology, p. 34; Cabot war diary, p. 12

events.words: Two large groups of unidentified planes closing.

A Judy "sneaking into the disposition under the cover of the interception" comes in on Cabot from astern, drops its bomb about 100 yd off her starboard quarter, loses a wing to gunfire and falls off her bow. Astoria calls it "tentatively ... a Zeke".
events.source: Cabot war diary, p. 12; North Carolina p. 5; Astoria pp. 64-66

events.words: Recovering CAP #2: 1st Lt. J. H. Carpenter missing, "last seen diving on an enemy aircraft during a dog fight following an interception".

events.original: 全機敵KdBニ突入セルモノト推定
events.translation: All aircraft presumed to have dived into the enemy carrier force.
events.note: The seven aircraft, 1230 to 1300. Results unknown. Planned bombing altitude 400 m.
events.source: 210th Air Group action report, form pp. 9 and 17

events.words: "1232 C/C to 020°T ... The SC-3 radar picked up bogey at 010°, distance 22 miles ... Fighters vectored out from task group merged with bogey on scope until raid had passed close aboard port beam."
"The sound of dog-fight and machine gun fire" is heard and tracked from the port bow to the beam. "A Judy or Zeke" is splashed 1,500 yards on the port quarter.

A Judy "appeared out of the clouds in a very steep dive" with a Corsair on each side. All three "pulled up sharply short of the water"; the Corsairs climbed into the cloud, and the Judy flattened out and "headed away from the ship". Speed increased to 25 knots.
events.source: Action report, p. 3; war diary p. 3

events.words: Fire opened at 1,500 yards, altitude 150 ft: 20 mm, 40 mm and 5-inch. The Judy turns to starboard, "wing over" and comes back at the ship. Its bomb, "released or ... knocked off in the turn", falls about 1,000 yards abeam.

"With wings at 45° angle, striking at 1250 Item" in the main radio transmitter room, abaft the bridge, at the twin 40 mm mount 41. A gasoline fireball goes through Main Radio, the 40 mm platform, CIC and plot.
Seven men are killed outright, five of them in or beside mount 41's crew (Report of Casualties, items 1-7).
events.source: Report of Casualties, action report p. 22; Irons, Phalanx, for mount 41's crew

events.words: "Seven dead, eleven critically wounded, fourteen slightly wounded." Fires under control in about ten minutes ("By 13??", overstruck), out in about fifty-five. Radio and radar out: she rejoins the group and is coached on station by other ships.
events.source: Haynsworth war diary, p. 4; action report pp. 3-5

events.words: "Out of a 15 plane enemy raid, 2 ZEKE's closed": a suicide Zeke in a shallow dive clips Cabot's SK radar antenna and explodes close aboard. Bunker Hill calls it "another JUDY". At 1302 Washington shoots down a suicide Zeke attacking Hancock.
events.source: Cabot p. 12; Astoria p. 72; Bunker Hill diary p. 8; VBF-6 history pp. 21-22

events.words: A friendly 5-inch shell hits North Carolina's No. 2 director: 3 killed, 44 wounded.

events.original: 敵空母×4見ユ 地點「スフ二イ」
events.translation: Four enemy carriers sighted, position 「スフ二イ」.
events.note: In column ス (129-20E to 129-40E, probable), the column that holds both TG 58.3 and TG 58.1 at noon. Row フ is not in the key, so the square is not plotted.
events.source: 252nd Air Group action report, message log p. 09

events.words: "At 1318 HAYNSWORTH was hit by suicide plane at number 41 twin 40 MM mount. All radar and radio out, 7 KIA, 14 WIA." After the hit Waldron takes station #1.
"At 1321 the U.S.S. HAYNSWORTH reported having received a bomb hit." Her radio was wrecked, so the report came late or by another ship.
22 enemy planes reported destroyed by CAP and gunfire. TG 58.3's report: a persistent 2-hour attack beginning at 1055; CAP shot down 19 and AA 3.
events.source: South Dakota war diary; TG 58.3 report p. 38

events.words: Second attack: two Suisei (Lt. 鈴木文夫) find nothing. The No. 2 plane's track chart survives: off Kokubu at 1410, farthest south at 1535 under rain cloud (cloud 10, base 500-900 m), north past Amami, Nakanoshima and Kuchinoerabu, landing at Tanegashima at 1750.
events.source: 210th track chart (別図第四), C13120082800 p. 12

events.words: A third-stage search plane reports a carrier force of four carriers at 「マキ三シ」 (row キ, 27-20N to 27-40N; column マ not in the key).

events.original: 空母×4見ユ 地點「メツ四セ」
events.translation: Four carriers sighted, position 「メツ四セ」.
events.note: The square 27-00N to 27-20N, 129-40E to 130-00E, the same square as the 0800 report. Haynsworth's track from her noon fix to her 2000 fix passes through it (a lead, not a record that she was seen).
events.source: 252nd Air Group action report, message log p. 09

events.words: Four Suisei of 第三御盾隊 take off against the carriers 85 nm east of northern Okinawa; one claims a battleship's stern at about 1835. Too late to be Haynsworth's attacker.
"At 1210 Hancock was hit by a suicide dive bomber."

"From 1240 to 1345 we picked up 8 men who had been blown into the water when Hancock was hit." The action report: she and four other destroyers dropped astern; of the eight, four were injured; a pair of low-flying Zekes made a pass at the rescue group, and her line of fire was blocked by another destroyer; the CAP splashed both.
events.source: Haynsworth war diary, p. 4; action report, p. 5

events.words: The dead are buried at sea, weighted with live 5-inch rounds (Irons, from crew diaries or letters; not in the war diary or action report).

"After clearing the Logistic Support Group, Task Group 58.3 stood to the northward to an operating area east of OKINAWA JIMA to give direct air support to the ground forces attacking enemy positions on OKINAWA JIMA. During the replenishment exercises the U.S.S. HANCOCK, CABOT, and HAYNSWORTH were detached from Task Group 58.3 and directed to return to the rear area for repairs and overhaul."

"At 1315 by authority CTF 58, 082125, we were detached from T.U. 58.3.4 and joined T.U. 58.3.10 proceeding to Ulithi. The T.U. consisted of Hancock, Cabot, Stemble and Haynsworth. OTC Captain Smith in Cabot."

"At 1355 we entered Ulithi Lagoon via Mugai Channel and T.U 58.3.10 was dissolved. After fueling from Sepulga in berth #303, we moored alongside Yosemite (AD19) in berth #319 for tender availability." Clocks were set to zone -10 at 0100.
"At 0612 we got underway for Pearl Harbor, T.H. via Eniwetok", speed of advance 20 knots; Pearl Harbor 27 April, Mare Island for repairs from 3 May.

claims.question: When was she hit?
claims.answer: 1250 Item
claims.source: Haynsworth action report, p. 3 (9 Apr 1945)
claims.note: "striking at 1250 Item". The ship's own report, three days after

claims.question: When was she hit?
claims.answer: Fires under control about 1300
claims.source: Haynsworth war diary, p. 4
claims.note: Typed "By13??" with an overstrike. Favours a hit before 1300

claims.question: When was she hit?
claims.source: COMDESRON 62 war diary, p. 8
claims.note: The squadron commander's diary, typed with no zone letter. Its line gives 7 killed and 14 wounded, where the ship's action report counts 27 wounded, so it was probably written from an early message: likely the time the news reached the squadron, not the hit (inferred). A zone slip can't explain it: 1250 to 1318 is 28 minutes

claims.question: When was she hit?
claims.answer: 1321 (report received)
claims.source: South Dakota war diary, 6 Apr
claims.note: "reported having received a bomb hit". Her radio was wrecked, so the report was late: this is when the news arrived, not when it happened

claims.question: What hit her?
claims.answer: A Judy (Suisei)
claims.source: Action report p. 3; war diary p. 3
claims.note: The ship called it a Judy throughout

claims.question: What hit her?
claims.answer: The engine was a two-row radial
claims.source: Ship's photo No. 26 (4228-45), in Irons, Phalanx
claims.note: Rules out a Suisei Model 11 or 12 (inline Atsuta). Fits a Model 33, and also a Zeke 52

claims.question: What hit her?
claims.answer: The machine gun was a 7.7 mm Type 97
claims.source: Ship's photo No. 27 (4824-45), in Irons, Phalanx
claims.note: The Suisei and the Zeke 52 both carried Type 97s in the cowling. Doesn't separate them

claims.question: What hit her?
claims.answer: "Blew his exterior bomb loose"
claims.source: XO Lothrop's letters, in Irons, Phalanx
claims.note: An external bomb sits better with a Zeke, whose bomb hung under the fuselage. Lothrop was in CIC

claims.question: What hit her?
claims.answer: Dived, pulled out, headed away, then turned back
claims.source: Action report, p. 3
claims.note: The pattern of a dive-bomber whose attack failed, not a Zeke on a crash run. Leans Judy

claims.question: What hit her?
claims.answer: The task group mixed up Judys and Zekes within the hour
claims.source: Bunker Hill diary p. 8; Astoria pp. 64-66
claims.note: Bunker Hill called the 1302 Zeke a Judy; Astoria called the 1226 Judy a Zeke. One ship's identification under fire is weak evidence

claims.question: Who flew it?
claims.answer: One of the 210th Air Group's seven
claims.source: Irons, Phalanx (uncited); 210th action report, form pp. 9, 17, 23
claims.note: Seven Suisei sent southeast of Tokunoshima, presumed to have dived in 1200-1300. Time, place and type agree. No Japanese record names a ship

claims.question: Who flew it?
claims.answer: One of the other 12 Suisei of Fifth Air Fleet
claims.source: Fifth Air Fleet operations record, pp. 11-13
claims.note: 23 Suisei went at TF 58 between 1015 and 1310; the 210th supplied 11. The 252nd's four have no launch time. Any that left after about 1120 couldn't have reached her by 1250

claims.question: Who flew it?
claims.answer: A bomb-carrying Zero
claims.source: Fifth Air Fleet record; Bennington, Hancock and Cabot reports
claims.note: 30 bomb-carrying Zeros went with the Suisei. They reached TF 58 at the same minutes: Bennington 1253, Hancock 1302, Cabot 1302

claims.question: How many died?
claims.answer: 7 killed outright
claims.source: War diary p. 4; action report p. 5; COMDESRON 62 p. 8
claims.note: The seven named on the Report of Casualties, items 1-7

claims.question: How many died?
claims.answer: 12 in all
claims.source: Action report, p. 5
claims.note: "five additional deaths" aboard South Dakota by 9 April. Irons agrees, and names four of the five; the fifth isn't found yet

claims.question: How many were wounded?
claims.source: War diary (11 + 14); action report (27); COMDESRON 62 (14); Irons, Phalanx (19)
claims.note: Counts made on different days and before or after the deaths aboard South Dakota

claims.question: Where did the bomb go?
claims.answer: "Released or ... knocked off in the turn", 1,000 yards abeam
claims.source: Action report, p. 3
claims.note: The ship wasn't sure which

claims.question: Where did the bomb go?
claims.answer: "One of our bursts blew his exterior bomb loose"
claims.source: Lothrop, in Irons, Phalanx

claims.question: Where did the bomb go?
claims.answer: "I did see the Japanese plane drop its bomb as it flew away from us"
claims.source: Weldon Powell (starboard quad 40 mm director), in Irons, Phalanx

claims.question: How many airmen died aboard?
claims.answer: One Japanese airman's body was found aboard
claims.source: Irons, Phalanx, from the crew
claims.note: Left alone for some time for fear it was booby-trapped. The action report and diary don't mention it

claims.question: How many airmen died aboard?
claims.answer: Every Suisei that day carried two men
claims.source: 210th crew list, form p. 23
claims.note: So a Judy should leave two. The second could have gone over the side with the wreckage, which was jettisoned. A Zero would leave one

claims.question: Where were the dead buried?
claims.answer: At sea, 7 April 1945, 1816
claims.source: Irons, Phalanx, from crew diaries
claims.note: Not in the war diary or action report

positions.label: First Kokubu airfield
positions.source: AMS L772 Kyushu 1:50,000, sheet 4242-III Kajiki (AMS 3, 1945), with 4242-II Kokubu
positions.note: Where the 210th's and the 252nd's Suisei took off. The open ground labelled "Airfield" between the Shin-kawa and Kawashiri, south of Kokubu, on the join of the two sheets; centre read off the sheet at 31°43.35'N 130°45.08'E (Tokyo datum, as printed), about ±400 m: the sheet draws the field's edge only as dashed tracks. Ticks: Kajiki's 31°45' tick and 31°40' neatline, its 130°45' tick beside the 130°45'10.4" neatline; Kokubu's 31°45' tick agrees within 0.1'. Read 28 Oct 2026; was hand-placed at 31.73, 130.76

positions.label: Second Kokubu airfield (Jūsantsuka-hara)
positions.source: AMS L772 Kyushu 1:50,000, sheet 4242-III Kajiki (AMS 3, 1945)
positions.note: Where the Type 99 Vals left from (vol. 17 p. 375). The field labelled "Airfield" at Jūsantsuka-hara, Mizobe-mura, NW of Kokubu, drawn as an outline lying NW-SE with revetments on its north side; centre read off the sheet at 31°47.55'N 130°43.75'E (Tokyo datum, as printed), about ±300 m. Ticks: the sheet's 31°50' and 31°40' neatlines and 31°45' tick, and the 130°45'10.4" east neatline (lon scale from both neatlines). Read 28 Oct 2026

positions.label: Kanoya airfield
positions.source: AMS L506 Japan 1:250,000, sheet NH 52-4 Kagoshima (Edition 1-AMS, compiled 1952, printed 1954: postwar edition)
positions.note: The landing-ground symbol "Kanoya Aux AB" SW of Kanoya town, read at 31°22.1'N 130°50.4'E, about ±0.3' (±600 m). Postwar edition: the 1:50,000 sheet that covers Kanoya (4241-II) was not available, and the 1952 sheet shows the field as it was then. Ticks: the graticule crosses at 31°30' and 31°15' on 130°45'; longitude from the 130°45' crosses with the scale from the sheet's width. Read 28 Oct 2026

positions.label: Izumi airfield
positions.source: AMS L772 Kyushu 1:50,000, sheet 4143-II Izumi (AMS 3, 1945)
positions.note: Where the Tsukuba and Yatabe air groups' thirteen Zeros took off at 0900 (o-izumi-0406). The rectangle labelled "Airfield" on the plain west of Izumi town, between Kawarayaki, Ichinoshime and the Kagoshima Main Line, drawn as an outline about 1.5 km square with no runways marked; centre read off the sheet at 32°05.14'N 130°19.42'E (Tokyo datum, as printed), about ±800 m (the outline's half-width). Corners from the four neatline corners (32°10', 32°00'; 130°15'10.4", 130°30'10.4"). About 313 nm from Haynsworth's noon fix. Read 28 Oct 2026

positions.label: Miyazaki airfield
positions.source: AMS L772 Kyushu 1:50,000, sheet 4342-I Miyazaki (AMS 3, 1945)
positions.note: "Miyazaki Airfield", by the coast south of Akae-kō and north of Hongō-kitakata and Akae-machi, drawn with two runways crossing (one WNW-ESE, one NW-SE) and buildings to the south; the point is the runways' crossing, read off the sheet at 31°52.43'N 131°26.66'E (Tokyo datum, as printed), about ±400 m (the runways run some 1.2 km either way). Corners from the four neatline corners (32°00', 31°50'; 131°15'10.4", 131°30'10.4"). About 314 nm from Haynsworth's noon fix. Read 28 Oct 2026

positions.label: Chiran airfield (Army)
positions.source: AMS L772 Kyushu 1:50,000, sheet 4141-II Kawanabe (AMS 3, 1945)
positions.note: The open ground labelled "Airfield" south-west of Chiran town, between Kambyu and Sendayama, drawn as an outline about 1.7 km across with buildings on its east side and no runways marked; centre read off the sheet at 31°21.27'N 130°25.68'E (Tokyo datum, as printed), about ±800 m. The sheet names only "Airfield": that this is the Army's Chiran field is inferred from the town beside it. Corners from the four neatline corners (31°30', 31°20'; 130°15'10.4", 130°30'10.4"). About 271 nm from Haynsworth's noon fix. Read 28 Oct 2026

positions.label: Bansei airfield (Army)
positions.source: AMS L772 Kyushu 1:50,000, sheet 4141-II Kawanabe (AMS 3, 1945)
positions.note: The diamond-shaped outline labelled "Airfield" on the coastal flat north-west of Kaseda, between Osaki, Shinkawa and the shore, about 1.5 km across, no runways marked; centre read off the sheet at 31°25.90'N 130°17.39'E (Tokyo datum, as printed), about ±700 m. The sheet names only "Airfield" (in Mansei-machi): that this is the Army's Bansei (万世) field is inferred from the township. Corners from the four neatline corners (31°30', 31°20'; 130°15'10.4", 130°30'10.4"). About 274 nm from Haynsworth's noon fix. Read 28 Oct 2026

positions.label: Miyakonojō airfield (Army)
positions.source: AMS L772 Kyushu 1:50,000, sheet 4342-III Miyakonojō (AMS 3, 1945)
positions.note: "Miyakonojo Airfield", the diamond-shaped outline west of the city between Shiriedu, Kumiki and Shimo-minahara, with buildings on its east side and "Army Barracks" and a drill ground south of it; centre read off the sheet at 31°43.96'N 131°02.37'E (Tokyo datum, as printed), about ±700 m. That this is the Army's Miyakonojō West (都城西) field is inferred from its place west of the city. A large unlabelled open area NE of Matsunomotochō, north of the city, may be another field (not entered). Corners from the four neatline corners (31°50', 31°40'; 131°00'10.4", 131°15'10.4"). About 300 nm from Haynsworth's noon fix. Read 28 Oct 2026

positions.label: メヘ一タ: 4 carriers heading south (first-stage search)

positions.note: Code 「メヘ一タ」: column メ (129-40E to 130-00E, good); row ヘ not in the okinawa-1945 key, so not plotted. 「敵ノ隊形ハ輪型陣ナリ 針路一七〇度 速力二四節」 (ring formation, course 170°, 24 kt), time 0845 on the intelligence message; the search plane's own line (T11 1段索 1/3Y, 「空母ヲ含ム敵部隊見ユ 空母×4 地點「メヘ一タ」 進行方向南 其ノ他十數隻」) has no time on this page. positions.label: サキ四セ: carriers (second-stage search)

positions.note: 20' grid square, decoded with kit/tools/jgrid.py (okinawa-1945 key: column サ good, row キ good); subdivision 四セ not decoded. A square, not a fix. 1130 is the plane's report (空母ヲ含ム敵部隊發見); the 252nd's log (p08) has 「敵空母二隻見ユ 地點「サキ四セ」」 and the 1154 order sends the Kokubu Suisei at the carriers there as of 1137. The square's centre is about 40 nm NE of Haynsworth's 1200 fix

positions.label: Izumi fighters sight a force: 徳之島ノ南方二十浬
